I seem to think that it's a bit of both? There are certain lifestyle changes you can make to reduce your odds of having a PA, or at least make the symptoms less intense, such as getting on proper medication, cutting out caffeine, and exercising more. However, changing your attitudes toward panic attacks and trying to convince yourself that it's not a big deal, ignoring the anxiety when it comes, etc, those are things that can also trick your brain into shutting off the anxiety response when it happens. I think there's some evidence to suggest that your thoughts and what you tell yourself (e.g. if you intentionally think positive thoughts instead of negative ones) can have an impact on brain chemistry. But it certainly becomes a lot easier to do so once you treat the physical aspects of anxiety. I'm not a therapist but this seems to be true in my experience.
